# Package `thaumcraft.api.machines`

[All packages](README.md)

What add-ons read from, and change in, four Thaumcraft machines: the Arcane Ear, the Brain in a Jar, the Deconstruction Table and the Arcane Bore.

Not a 1.7.10 package. The ComputerCraft and OpenComputers peripherals of Thaumic Tinkerer read the public fields of the internal block entities (`TileSensor.note`, `TileJarBrain.xp`, `TileDeconstructionTable.aspect`, `TileArcaneBore.hasFocus` ...); the block entities of this port implement these interfaces instead, so an add-on asks `level.getBlockEntity(pos) instanceof IArcaneEar ear`. Each interface holds exactly what those peripherals read or wrote. Thaumcraft's own block entities are the only implementations; Thaumcraft never asks an add-on's block entity for them.

The getters read the block entity's own state and change nothing; on a client they read the copy the server syncs. Call them on the thread that owns the level (the server thread for a server block entity).

Types: [`IArcaneBore`](#iarcanebore), [`IArcaneEar`](#iarcaneear), [`IBrainJar`](#ibrainjar), [`IDeconstructor`](#ideconstructor)

## IArcaneBore

```java
public interface IArcaneBore
```

The Arcane Bore (block `thaumcraft:arcane_bore`, the original `TileArcaneBore`): its two tools and what they make of it.

The bore digs while it is powered by redstone and holds an Excavation focus (slot 0) and a pickaxe (slot 1) that is not worn down to its last point. Each method answers one question of the original peripheral `tt_arcanebore` (`hasPickaxe`, `hasFocus`, `isPickaxeBroken`, `isWorking`, `getRadius`, `getSpeed`, `hasNativeClusters`, `getFortune`, `hasSilkTouch`), with the original formula.

The tools are saved with the block and synced to clients, so the item questions answer on both sides; `isPowered()` and `isWorking()` read the redstone around the bore and its base, which a client knows only as far as its own copy of the world goes. Read-only: nothing here changes the bore.

<a id="iarcanebore-hasfocus"></a>
```java
boolean hasFocus()
```

Whether slot 0 holds a usable Excavation focus (original `hasFocus`).

**Returns:** true for an Excavation focus with upgrades this version supports

<a id="iarcanebore-haspickaxe"></a>
```java
boolean hasPickaxe()
```

Whether slot 1 holds a pickaxe (original `hasPickaxe`), whatever its wear.

**Returns:** true for a single pickaxe

<a id="iarcanebore-getpickaxe"></a>
```java
ItemStack getPickaxe()
```

A copy of the stack in the pickaxe slot (original `getStackInSlot(1)`); changing it changes nothing in the bore.

**Returns:** the pickaxe, or `ItemStack.EMPTY`

<a id="iarcanebore-ispickaxebroken"></a>
```java
boolean isPickaxeBroken()
```

Whether the pickaxe is worn down to its last point (original peripheral `isPickaxeBroken`: damage + 1 equals the maximum damage). The bore does not dig with such a pickaxe, so that it never breaks.

**Returns:** true for a pickaxe one use from breaking; false without a pickaxe

<a id="iarcanebore-ispowered"></a>
```java
boolean isPowered()
```

Whether the bore or its base receives redstone power (original `gettingPower()`). False for a bore that is not in a loaded, current block of its level; the call never loads a chunk.

**Returns:** true when powered

<a id="iarcanebore-isworking"></a>
```java
boolean isWorking()
```

Whether the bore is able to dig now (original peripheral `isWorking`): powered, with a focus, and with a damageable pickaxe that is not worn down to its last point. A bore whose saved data could not be read (it keeps the data untouched and does not dig) answers false. It does not say whether there is a block in reach to dig.

**Returns:** true when the bore can work

<a id="iarcanebore-getradius"></a>
```java
int getRadius()
```

The radius of the hole the bore digs around its axis: 2 plus the Enlarge upgrades of the focus (original `maxRadius + area`). The original peripheral's `getRadius` answered the width of the hole, `1 + 2 * getRadius()`.

**Returns:** the radius in blocks

<a id="iarcanebore-getspeed"></a>
```java
int getSpeed()
```

The dig speed: the Potency upgrades of the focus plus the Efficiency level of the pickaxe (original `speed`).

**Returns:** the speed bonus, zero without either

<a id="iarcanebore-hasnativeclusters"></a>
```java
boolean hasNativeClusters()
```

Whether the pickaxe is the Pickaxe of the Core (`thaumcraft:elemental_pickaxe`), whose special mining turns ores into native clusters (original peripheral `hasNativeClusters`).

**Returns:** true for the Pickaxe of the Core

<a id="iarcanebore-getpickaxefortune"></a>
```java
int getPickaxeFortune()
```

The Fortune level of the pickaxe's own enchantments (original peripheral `getFortune`). The bore digs with the higher of this and the Treasure upgrades of its focus.

**Returns:** the Fortune level, zero without a pickaxe

<a id="iarcanebore-hassilktouch"></a>
```java
boolean hasSilkTouch()
```

Whether the pickaxe has Silk Touch (original peripheral `hasSilkTouch`).

**Returns:** true for a pickaxe with Silk Touch

## IArcaneEar

```java
public interface IArcaneEar
```

The Arcane Ear (block `thaumcraft:arcane_ear`, the original `TileSensor`): the note it listens for.

The ear gives a ten-tick redstone pulse when a note block within 64 blocks plays its note on its instrument (the instrument comes from the block under the ear and is not part of this interface). A right click raises the note by one and wraps from 24 to 0. The original peripheral `tt_arcaneear` read and wrote the public field `note`.

<a id="iarcaneear-min_note"></a>
```java
int MIN_NOTE
```

The lowest note, F#3 (the note block's 0).

<a id="iarcaneear-max_note"></a>
```java
int MAX_NOTE
```

The highest note, F#5 (the note block's 24).

<a id="iarcaneear-getnote"></a>
```java
int getNote()
```

The note the ear listens for, `#MIN_NOTE` to `#MAX_NOTE`, in note block clicks. Saved with the block (key `note`) and synced to clients. Either side.

**Returns:** the note

<a id="iarcaneear-setnote"></a>
```java
void setNote(int note)
```

Tunes the ear to a note, with the effects of tuning it by hand: the note is saved with the block and sent to the clients that see it. Unlike the right click it does not play the note (neither did the original peripheral). Setting the note the ear already has changes nothing.

Server side only, on the server thread: on a client copy, and on an ear that is not placed in a level, it does nothing.

**Throws:** `IllegalArgumentException` — for a note outside 0..24 (the original peripheral stored any byte; the ear never hears such a note, and a save of the port reads it back as the nearest of 0..24)

**Throws:** `IllegalStateException` — when the ear is in a server level and this is not the server thread

**Parameters:**
- `note` — the new note, `#MIN_NOTE` to `#MAX_NOTE`

## IBrainJar

```java
public interface IBrainJar
```

The Brain in a Jar (block `thaumcraft:jar_brain`, the original `TileJarBrain`): the experience it holds.

The jar pulls experience orbs within six blocks towards itself and swallows those inside its block, up to `getXpMax()`. The original peripheral `tt_braininajar` read the public field `xp`.

<a id="ibrainjar-getxp"></a>
```java
int getXp()
```

The stored experience points (not levels). Saved with the block (key `XP`) and synced to clients when it changes. It can exceed `getXpMax()` for the rest of the tick in which the jar swallowed several orbs at once; the next server tick cuts it back to the maximum, as the original did. Either side.

**Returns:** the stored experience, at least zero

<a id="ibrainjar-getxpmax"></a>
```java
int getXpMax()
```

The most experience the jar keeps: 2000 (original `xpMax`). Either side.

**Returns:** the capacity in experience points

## IDeconstructor

```java
public interface IDeconstructor
```

The Deconstruction Table (block `thaumcraft:deconstruction_table`, the original `TileDeconstructionTable`): its input and the primal it found.

The table breaks one item of its input every forty ticks; with a chance it yields one primal aspect, which waits on the table until a player takes it as a research point. While a primal waits the table does not work. The original peripheral `tt_deconstructor` read the public field `aspect` and the stack in slot 0.

<a id="ideconstructor-getreward"></a>
```java
Aspect getReward()
```

The primal aspect waiting to be taken (original `aspect`), or `null` when there is none. Saved with the block (key `Aspect`) and synced to clients. Either side.

**Returns:** one of the six primal aspects, or `null`

<a id="ideconstructor-hasitem"></a>
```java
boolean hasItem()
```

Whether an item lies in the input slot (original `getStackInSlot(0) != null`). A table whose saved data could not be read keeps that data untouched and answers false. Either side.

**Returns:** true when the input slot holds an item
